elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services infringe third-party intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The only purported SFJ-performance IP language is an unnumbered fragment placed after “caused by (i) the gross negligence or willful misconduct of any” and is not grammatically connected to SFJ's indemnity obligation. Operative subsection (f) instead addresses infringement by the Product or PB's performance.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging that the deliverables infringe third-party intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The clause does not identify deliverables as covered. “Product” is not shown to mean Vendor deliverables, and the appended SFJ infringement fragment is not operatively integrated into the indemnity triggers.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are included as beneficiaries of Vendor's indemnity.
elements.evidence: “PB Indemnified Parties” expressly includes PB and its Affiliates, together with their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents.

elements.element: Vendor defends Customer and its affiliates against all covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: SFJ agrees to “indemnify and hold” the PB Indemnified Parties harmless, but there is no duty to defend.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The clause covers SFJ's breach of provisions of the AZ License, but not breach of applicable law generally.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No data-breach indemnity trigger appears.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) covers third-party claims arising from SFJ's or its related parties' gross negligence in performing SFJ's obligations.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subsection (a) covers third-party claims arising from SFJ's or its related parties' “willful misconduct” in performing SFJ's obligations.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires Customer to notify Vendor of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No notice procedure appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure gives Vendor control of the defense and settlement of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No defense-control or settlement-control provision appears.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires Customer to cooperate with Vendor in defending a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears.

elements.element: No Customer indemnity extends beyond claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No operative PB-to-SFJ indemnity is included in the rendered clause, so the condition for restricting such an indemnity is demonstrably absent. References to PB conduct remain triggers for SFJ's indemnity and do not reverse the indemnity direction.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services infringe third-party intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The appended SFJ-performance infringement language is a sentence fragment embedded in the exception and does not operate as an indemnity trigger.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging that the deliverables infringe third-party intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Deliverables are not expressly covered, and the clause does not establish that the referenced Product constitutes Vendor deliverables.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by Customer's modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specification exclusion appears.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No procure-right remedy appears.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must modify the affected services or deliverables to make them non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must replace the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing equivalents.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears.

elements.element: If the other infringement remedies are unavailable, Vendor must refund the applicable fees.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability is subject to a super-cap equal to three times the annual fees.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no liability cap or reference to three times annual fees.

result.reason: Neither position is satisfied. Although the clause covers PB affiliates and SFJ's gross negligence and willful misconduct, it omits defense, general breach-of-law and data-breach coverage, procedures, fallback exclusions, infringement remedies, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap. Most critically, the added SFJ IP language follows the incomplete phrase “gross negligence or willful misconduct of any” without numbering or a connecting indemnity trigger, rendering it grammatically inoperative and creating ambiguity rather than the intended Vendor IP indemnity. Because no complete level is reached and the redline introduces a malformed exception, it is neither minimal nor intent-preserving.
